nodes.summary: For every linearly ordered field $R$ with a floor function, bucket sort applied to the empty array of elements of $R$ returns the empty array at zero cost.
nodes.title: Bucket sort on the empty array

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}$ be independent random variables, each uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$. For $i < n$, let $N_i$ be the number of indices $j < n$ with $\lfloor n \omega_j \rfloor = i$. Then $\mathbb{E}[N_i] = 1$.
nodes.title: Expected occupancy of a bucket in bucket sort

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}$ be independent random variables, each uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$. For $i < n$, let $N_i$ be the number of indices $j < n$ with $\lfloor n \omega_j \rfloor = i$. Then $\mathbb{E}[N_i^2] = 2 - 1/n$.
nodes.title: Second moment of a bucket's occupancy in bucket sort

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}$ be independent random variables, each uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$. For $i < n$, let $N_i$ be the number of indices $j < n$ with $\lfloor n \omega_j \rfloor = i$. Then $\operatorname{Var}(N_i) = 1 - 1/n$.
nodes.title: Variance of a bucket's occupancy in bucket sort

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function. For every array of elements of $R$ that all lie in $[0, 1)$, the array returned by bucket sort is a permutation of the input: every element occurs in the output exactly as many times as in the input.
nodes.title: Bucket sort permutes its input

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function. For every array of elements of $R$ that all lie in $[0, 1)$, the array returned by bucket sort is nondecreasing: each entry is at most every entry after it.
nodes.title: Bucket sort sorts

nodes.summary: For each $n$, let $\omega = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ have independent coordinates, each uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$. Let $T_n(\omega)$ be the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the array $(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ if every $\omega_j$ lies in $[0, 1)$, and $T_n(\omega) = 0$ otherwise. Then $\mathbb{E}[T_n] = \Theta(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Bucket sort runs in expected linear time

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $\omega = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ have independent coordinates, each uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$. Let $T(\omega)$ be the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the array $(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ if every $\omega_j$ lies in $[0, 1)$, and $T(\omega) = 0$ otherwise. Then $5n \le \mathbb{E}[T]$.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the expected time of bucket sort

nodes.summary: Let $\omega_0$ be uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$, and let $T(\omega_0)$ be the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the one-element array $(\omega_0)$ if $\omega_0 \in [0, 1)$, and $T(\omega_0) = 0$ otherwise. Then $\mathbb{E}[T] = 5$.
nodes.title: Expected time of bucket sort on one input

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $\omega = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ have independent coordinates, each uniformly distributed on $[0, 1)$. Let $T(\omega)$ be the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the array $(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ if every $\omega_j$ lies in $[0, 1)$, and $T(\omega) = 0$ otherwise. Then $\mathbb{E}[T] \le 5n + (n - 1)/2$.
nodes.title: Upper bound on the expected time of bucket sort

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the empty array, the only input of length $n = 0$. Its expectation under the product of zero copies of the uniform distribution on $[0, 1)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Bucket sort on the empty input has expected time zero

nodes.summary: For every $n$, let $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ map $\omega = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ to the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the array $(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ if every $\omega_j$ lies in $[0, 1)$, and to $0$ otherwise. Then $T$ is integrable with respect to the product of $n$ copies of the uniform distribution on $[0, 1)$.
nodes.title: The running time of bucket sort is integrable

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function and let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be an array of elements of $R$ that all lie in $[0, 1)$. For $0 \le i < n$ let $c_i$ be the number of indices $j$ with $\lfloor n x_j \rfloor = i$. Then the cost of bucket sort on this array is at most $5n + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} c_i^2$.
nodes.title: Bound on the cost of bucket sort via squared bucket sizes

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function. For every array of $n$ elements of $R$ that all lie in $[0, 1)$, the cost of bucket sort on this array is at least $5n$.
nodes.title: Linear lower bound on the cost of bucket sort

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the function $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ that maps $\omega = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ to the number of time steps that bucket sort charges on the array $(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})$ if every $\omega_j$ lies in $[0, 1)$, and to $0$ otherwise, is measurable.
nodes.title: The running time of bucket sort is measurable

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function and let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be an array of elements of $R$ that all lie in $[0, 1)$. For $0 \le i < n$ let $B_i$ be the list of the entries $x_j$ with $\lfloor n x_j \rfloor = i$, in decreasing order of $j$, and let $T(B_i)$ be the number of comparisons insertion sort makes on $B_i$. nodes.title: Exact cost of bucket sort

If $n = 0$, bucket sort returns the empty array at zero cost. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
